label: b-gradient-4x3
_why: THE B GRADIENT (user-ruled 2026-09-22: "Assuming anchor cost and mild spending set, go with four n=3 runs that will allow to create a clean gradient on B, if it exists", then "the metrics are world GDP (target 1.0 of vanilla) and British U* (target 15%)"). Four configs at B 1.52 / 1.55 / 1.58 / 1.62, three seeds each, on the probe-slide-mild base — which is already measured at B 1.50 with n=5 and joins as a free fifth point.
_the_base_is_fixed: anchor-slide + --anchor-cost + C 1.9 + in0 1.2 + A 2.2 + the MILD spending set (0.95 / 1.0 / 2.0) + the 24-month bar. PROVED per book before launch: output_qty, building_cost and ai_value are byte-identical to probe-slide-mild across all 56 rungs, ai_defines identical, and only `inputs` (41 rungs) and `target_be` move. ⇒ B is the ONLY thing that varies across the five points.

_the_model_it_tests.world_gdp: GDP(B) = 1.16 − 5.32 · ln(B/1.5). The slope comes from two independent routes agreeing to 12%: (A) costslide → accel-slide, inputs ONLY changed, with the accel ladder 1/1.5/2.6/4.7 converted to an equivalent uniform B_eff = 1.642 by matching Σw·ln(m) / Σw·e over the tiered workforce weights → −4.98; (B) the pre-slide canon → b18-gm step de-confounded for its cost gain-match using the pre-slide cost slope (−2.44 per ln cost) → −5.65. Central −5.32.
_the_model_it_tests.british_U: logit(GBR U*) = −2.9031 + 22.45 · ln(B/1.5), U* = 1/(1+e^−logit). One clean pure-input step: costslide 5.4, 1.7 → median 3.55%; accel 23.0, 20.7 → median 21.85%. ⚠ LOGIT, not linear: Britain sits near the FLOOR (5.2% at B 1.50), not near 50% where the two links coincide — a linear fit predicts NEGATIVE U* below B 1.46.
_the_model_it_tests.the_targets: world GDP 1.00 → B 1.546. British U* 15% → B 1.580. They are 2% apart in B and both are essentially met near B 1.56 (GDP 0.95, U* 11.7%).

_predictions._basis: The two formulae above, anchored on probe-slide-mild at n=5 (world GDP median 1.16, British U* median 5.2%). Stated before launch as the no-ceteris-paribus rule requires. ⚠ §10.83.7: these are DIRECTIONS with magnitudes and the magnitudes are the weak half.
_predictions.the_two_targets_are_BRACKETED: world GDP 1.00 falls between B 1.52 and 1.55; British U* 15% falls between B 1.55 and 1.62. Both are interpolated, not extrapolated, and they stay bracketed under ±30% error on either slope.
_predictions.gradient_exists: PREDICT a monotone fall in world GDP and a monotone rise in British U* across the four. ⭐ THE NULL THIS BATCH CAN RETURN: a slope shallower than ~4 on GDP would not be distinguishable from flat at this spacing, and 'the gradient does not exist' is then the answer.
_predictions.hard_lines: PREDICT no run broken. At the central slope the four sit 1.09 / 0.99 / 0.88 / 0.75, all inside the 0.66–1.38 hard band; at a 30% steeper slope B 1.62 lands at 0.63 and would break by stall.
_predictions.britain_disintegration: PREDICT no discard. Across all 12 post-slide runs measured to date, British GDP ÷ vanilla's 1935 median (£388M) runs 0.86–2.11 — the 0.20 floor has never been approached.

_the_discard_rule: USER-RULED 2026-09-22: a run whose Britain disintegrates — British GDP at 1935 below 20% of the vanilla n=16 median, i.e. below £78M — is DISCARDED from the gradient, not counted as a data point. It has never yet bound (closest: accel run 1 at 0.86), so it is a safety net against a pathological seed rather than a live constraint. ⚠ This is separate from the register's own hard lines: a run can be BROKEN (stall/runoff) and still be a valid point on the B gradient, because a broken run still carries a GDP and a British U*.
_power: SE of a median of 3 ≈ 1.25σ/√3 = 0.165 (σ 0.228, the register's fixed within-config spread). Over the five ln B points Sxx = 0.00375, so SE(GDP slope) = 2.69 and the predicted −5.32 lands at t ≈ 2.0. ⚠ That is enough to confirm a slope this steep EXISTS, not to pin its value. Widening the outer points to 1.48 / 1.66 would restore t ≈ 3 at the cost of spending two configs far from anything wanted; bracketing the targets was judged worth more, since the point is to FIND B rather than to characterise B.
_watch: run 1 of each config at ~5 min: marker, version, error window BY POSITION, clock, queue_mix
each endpoint: British U* and British GDP ÷ £388M (the discard test), then criteria.mjs for the HARD lines
at the end: the five-point regression of world GDP on ln B and of logit(GBR U*) on ln B
post-batch: preflight -Session, VERDICT.md, the SESSION_VERDICTS row, FINDINGS
_caveats: THE BRITISH U* SLOPE RESTS ON ONE STEP, costslide → accel, n=2 against n=2 with a broken run on each side. The GDP slope has two corroborating routes; this one does not.
The slope was measured on CANON-spending books and is applied to a MILD-spending base (which shifted Britain 3.55% → 5.20% at the same B). The shift is small but the transfer is an assumption.

Neither formula says anything about the OTHER shortlist countries. Measured over 12 post-slide runs, the within-run spread across members is 49–77pp against a 40pp band, and B is a pure location lever (it moved GBR +18.5, USA +15.5, FRA +13.5pp) — so no B fixes the dispersion. This batch deliberately targets Britain alone, on the user's instruction.
Launch ONLY through tools/testbed/launch_detached.ps1 CALLED DIRECTLY from the PowerShell tool (landmine L30); the STOP file must be absent.

Arm the watcher with the session NAME, not a path, and confirm tools/testbed/sessions/<stamp>/stop_watch.log exists ~90s later (the 2026-09-21 landmine). ⚠ Its GDP fallback is raised to 1.4 so a criteria.mjs failure cannot kill a gradient batch on a config whose predicted GDP is 1.09.
_run_order: Each config's three runs BACK TO BACK (the 2026-09-13 no-alternation ruling), in ascending B so the first completed config is the one nearest the current anchor and any surprise shows early.
